name: Joseph Smith
role: Founder of the Latter Day Saint movement; mayor of Nauvoo and 1844 presidential candidate (1805-1844)
summary: Joseph Smith combined a religious movement with civic ambitions: he praised the Constitution and the American founders, ran in 1844 for gradual compensated emancipation, prison reform, a smaller Congress, a national bank, a tariff and continental expansion, and defended religious liberty. He also led a communal consecration system for the poor, ruled Nauvoo as mayor and militia commander, planned a theocratic Kingdom of God, taught plural marriage, and ordered the Expositor press destroyed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Defended property and sought redress for the Saints' lost Missouri lands through the Constitution, but the early law of consecration put property under church bishops, so the evidence is mixed.

state-harmful.rationale: Treated government as needed and divinely sanctioned: called the Constitution a heavenly banner founded in the wisdom of God and proposed reforms to government rather than its removal.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wanted the president given full power to send an army to suppress mobs and a navy to watch the coasts, while also urging cuts in the pay, number and power of government officers.

decide-locally.rationale: Defended states' reserved rights and Nauvoo's chartered self-rule, but his platform also asked for federal power to suppress mobs over the head of a governor.

rehabilitation.rationale: Urged legislators to make penalties for larceny and felonies work on roads and public works where the culprit can be taught wisdom and virtue, and to turn penitentiaries into seminaries of learning; rigor and seclusion would not reform as well as reason and friendship.

traditional-family.rationale: Taught marriage as ordained of God, eternal family sealing and a husband's headship, but also introduced plural marriage, so the evidence for a conventional family is mixed.

more-religion-public.rationale: His platform opens by calling the people to 'turn unto the Lord and live, and reform this nation', and he planned a Kingdom of God with a Council of Fifty.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Welcomed immigrants and gathered converts from abroad to Nauvoo; the platform welcomes people of every color, clime and tongue.

free-trade.rationale: His platform backs a protective tariff for domestic industry and says nothing in favour of free trade, so he leaned against it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The 1844 platform calls it the highest point of supervision to protect agriculture, manufactures, navigation and commerce by a judicious tariff.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Explicitly urged Congress to grant a national central bank with branches in every state and territory.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Platform praises bursting the chains of oppression and monarchy and fears a virtual monarchy; he was himself later made king in the Council of Fifty, which was not hereditary.

democracy-best.rationale: Praised the elective American government and said the people are the sovereign, but also held that man cannot govern himself and favored a divine theocracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revelations he dictated permit war when God commands it and allow defence of one's life, and he defended armed self-defence in Missouri; he also counselled patience under repeated attack.

separate-church-state.rationale: Served at once as church president and mayor and planned a theocratic kingdom, yet quoted Madison on exempting the functions of religion from civil jurisdiction and defended religious liberty for all.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Described ancient Israel's theocracy approvingly, with God making laws, and organized a Kingdom of God, yet Nauvoo ordinances and his platform rest on the Constitution.

military-superiority.rationale: Platform endorsed Washington's maxim that being prepared for war is a means of preserving peace and wanted a navy watching the coasts.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His platform welcomes neighbors from any state or country 'of whatever color, clime or tongue' and invites all the world to unite as one great family.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Said the Union should extend to Oregon only when the red man's consent is obtained.

restore-past-order.rationale: Platform pledges to walk the old paths of the founders and cites Harrison's aim to restore the government to its pristine health; his church claims to restore the primitive gospel.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The law of consecration he dictated gave each family a portion according to its circumstances, wants and needs, with equal claims on common stewardship property. It applied inside the church, not as state policy, and the idle were not to eat.

national-rebirth.rationale: Platform says the republic has declined since Van Buren and calls the people to turn to the Lord and reform the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Platform says the Union should spread from the east to the west sea, take in Texas, Mexico and Canada, and the Teachings quote him: 'We should grasp all the territory we can.'

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Preached that Judah must return and Jerusalem be rebuilt and a revelation he dictated says Judah is to flee to Jerusalem; this is stated as prophecy, not as a political right to statehood.

rule-by-example.rationale: Platform urges rendering good for evil and making honor the standard, and says reason and friendship reform better than rigor.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Built his movement on revelation and faith as a principle of action rather than reason alone.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Secondhand remarks attributed to him favor separation by law of Black and white people, while his 1844 platform says the Constitution knows no color; the record conflicts.

national-mission.rationale: Platform invites Texas, Mexico, Canada and 'all the world' to join the Union and calls the Constitution a heavenly banner founded in the wisdom of God.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Platform describes wicked and designing men unrobing government, corrupt legislation and politicians whose motto is 'Every man has his price'.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He is reported to have opposed Black-white marriages, fining people in two Nauvoo cases; the report is secondhand.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1844 platform says the Constitution means just what it says without reference to color or condition, urges officers to ameliorate the condition of 'black or white, bond or free', and cites that God made all nations of one blood. Earlier remarks and the curse-of-Ham readings cut the other way, so the later platform is taken.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The platform says 'the people are the government, and their united voice is the only sovereign that should rule'.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Revelations he dictated require the church to remember the poor and needy first: surplus is consecrated to a storehouse for them, and those who do not impart their abundance are condemned.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Declared martial law in Nauvoo and mobilized the Legion in June 1844 after the Expositor affair; this was a city emergency, not a national one.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Proposed paying members of Congress two dollars a day and board, which he said is more than the farmer gets but is honest.

clerical-rule.rationale: Taught that the priesthood is a perfect law of theocracy and held civil and church office at once, but his platform defers to the elected people.

death-penalty.rationale: His platform says murder alone can claim confinement or death.

central-bank-independence.rationale: His proposed national bank would have its directors elected yearly by the people and the people made controllers of its ways and means, not insulated from elected control.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Revelations he dictated describe the earth and all things as God's and property as a stewardship; the rich are told to impart to the poor and the poor are to be exalted as the rich are made low.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Held church and civil authority together as mayor and church president and described the priesthood as a theocracy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Platform says that after Democratic, Whig and pseudo-Whig presidents it is time to have a President of the United States, and he ran on an independent platform.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Platform asks that the president be given full power to send an army to suppress mobs, invasion or rebellion without a governor's request, and deplores the South Carolina rebellion.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Said no man may take life over differences of religion and that governments should permit every man to enjoy his religion unmolested; the Articles of Faith allow all men to worship how, where or what they may.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Told the Saints to keep importuning for redress under the laws and Constitution, but moved them from Ohio, Missouri and Illinois and planned a move west.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: His motto in the Teachings says woe to tyrants, aristocracy and tories, and his platform mocks the nobility of nations.

public-money-creation.rationale: Proposed a national bank whose capital is held by the nation and whose bills may not exceed its capital, with officers elected yearly; he wanted to end brokerage and keep the people's money in their own pockets.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Called the Constitution a heavenly banner and a charter of equal rights that safeguards conscience and the press.

elective-rulers.rationale: Platform says the people are the government and officers their servants; he ran for president himself.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Platform urges voters to hurl from office candidates who break their promises and says a governor who becomes a mobber should be punished; yet revelations bid the Saints be subject to the powers that be.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: On Zion's Camp he told men to leave rattlesnakes alone and not to kill birds or animals except to avoid hunger, and a revelation says woe to those who waste flesh needlessly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Revelations he dictated say beasts and fowls are ordained for food and raiment, used sparingly, and warn against wasting flesh.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A revelation he dictated says 'Wo unto you rich men, that will not give your substance to the poor' and that those who take the abundance and impart not to the poor will lift up their eyes in hell.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Revelations he dictated say to be subject to the powers that be and let no man break the laws of the land; the Articles of Faith affirm obeying, honoring and sustaining the law. He did resist Missouri authorities.

religion-illusion.rationale: Presented religion as truth and revelation from God, not illusion.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Organized Zion and the early United Order as communities with shared stewardship, but warned in the 1830s against organizing on common-stock principles, and Nauvoo was a conventional chartered city.

suppress-opposition.rationale: With the Nauvoo council he declared the Expositor a nuisance and ordered its press destroyed in June 1844 and declared martial law; the platform and his earlier writings, however, praise freedom of the press. The most recent act is taken.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Wrote that no man is authorized to take life over religious difference, that all governments ought to tolerate and protect religion, and that everyone has a constitutional right to be a false prophet as well as a true one.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: His platform says the people are the government and their united voice the only sovereign; his sermons call the priesthood a perfect law of theocracy that stands as God to give laws.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Platform endorses preparedness for war, a navy and a patriotic militia, and he led the Nauvoo Legion.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Urged the nation to turn to the Lord and held religion central to public life.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called for opening prisons, abolishing the cruel customs of prisons and pardoning convicts, but kept confinement or death for murder and did not address police.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Organized the Relief Society and said the sisters were ordained in their offices, yet ordained men only to the priesthood quorums.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The revelation on marriage he dictated requires a wife to administer to her husband in plural marriage or be destroyed, and the Teachings call the husband head of the wife.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Revelations he dictated say the idler shall not eat the bread or wear the garments of the laborer, tying maintenance to work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A revelation he dictated says that if an enemy seeks a man's life and endangers it, the enemy is delivered into his hands and he is justified.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The platform calls on the people to turn to the Lord, frustrate the designs of wicked men and make honor the standard; a revelation says when the wicked rule the people mourn.

second-chamber.rationale: His plan to shrink Congress keeps two senators per state alongside members chosen by population.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Platform opens with anxiety for all men's happiness 'both in time and in eternity', and he taught that temporal and spiritual are one.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: A revelation he dictated says to renounce war and proclaim peace and that war may be waged only after a standard of peace is lifted three times; the platform quotes Madison for amicable discussion over arms.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Said truth should be received from wherever it comes and that he would unite men of all denominations in love, but a revelation he dictated calls his the only true and living church.

premarital-sex.rationale: Revelations he dictated forbid adultery and lustful looking and call for cleaving to one's wife only; sex outside marriage is not countenanced.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Articles of Faith say the Bible is the word of God only as far as it is translated correctly; he also revised it and added further scripture.

national-church-status.rationale: Claimed equal rights for Presbyterians, Baptists and Catholics and defended all denominations against persecution, and the Articles of Faith allow all men to worship as they may.

notes: Records only what he said in the 1844 platform, his letters and sermons as compiled in the Teachings, and revelations he dictated, taken as his words. Statements on Black people and the Nauvoo Expositor rely partly on later or secondary accounts and are low confidence. His views on slavery moved from defending slaveholders' rights in the 1830s to urging compensated abolition in 1844; the latter is used.
